summary: Backend regression + new-endpoint validation for parallelized competitor matching/pricing (ThreadPoolExecutor). All 35 pytest tests pass (34 previously + 8 new for iteration 13, 1 previous skip-only that now passes with wider limit) covering every endpoint listed in the review request: products listing/filters/pagination, price-settings, category-rules (with new auto_update_ikas field), dashboard, scan-all/scan-status/scan-stop, price-changes, price-changes-full (with pagination/status_filter/search), apply-price (404 invalid slug + floor/purchase safety check + missing ikas_id), auto-match (non-blocking task_key + status polling), auto-match-category (404 for unknown, task_key + progress fields for real category), match-status (running/unknown task), check-price (404 when no matches, task_key + non-blocking when matched), check-price-status. Backend starts cleanly after competitor_pricing.py parallelization changes (no import/startup errors). All background endpoints return task_key in <1s confirming non-blocking behavior. ScraperAPI actual scraping intentionally NOT tested per instructions.

minor.issue: match_status filter is applied POST-pagination (in-memory filter after $skip/$limit aggregation). Result: (1) `total` field returns unfiltered count (e.g. 4186 for unmatched even though most products are matched); (2) small `limit` values return 0 products despite `total>0` (limit=1→0 results, limit=5→0, limit=20→3, limit=100→83); (3) `pages` count is wrong for filtered views. Frontend pagination on unmatched/matched views will be misleading. See competitor_routes.py L487 (count) vs L535-539 (post-filter). Fix: push the match_status filter into the Mongo aggregation using $lookup on competitor_matches then $match on match_count.

critical_code_review_comments: competitor_routes.py is now 1437 lines. Split into competitor_products.py / competitor_matching.py / competitor_pricing_routes.py / competitor_scan.py / competitor_apply.py — same recommendation as iter-11/12.
In list_products_enhanced (L468-555), match_status filter is applied AFTER $skip/$limit in the aggregation. This is a functional bug (see minor issue above), not just a style concern.
_run_category_match (L166-240) and _run_price_check use `asyncio.get_event_loop()` inside a coroutine — deprecated on 3.10+. Use `asyncio.get_running_loop()`.

_run_category_match writes `products_matched` and `total_matches` fields on system_status but the initial upsert (L157-161) sets only `progress:0/matched:0` — these two fields do NOT exist until the first product is processed. The match-status endpoint therefore returns partial shape in the first few ms after task creation. Test still passes (uses set-intersection) but frontends should defensively default to 0.

apply-price still returns HTTP 200 with success:false for business errors (no floor, no ikas_id, no variant, no price list, no fx rate). Consider 422/409 so frontend can differentiate transport vs domain errors — recurring comment from iter-12.

check-price endpoint duplicates logic in scan-all's per-product path (scrape_all_competitor_prices → update products.cheapest_competitor_price + insert price_history). Refactor into a shared helper to avoid drift.

PriceSettingsRequest only SETS floor_price/purchase_price when non-None (L382-385). There is no way to CLEAR either value via API — needed for correct floor-check flow if the operator entered a wrong number.

No pytest cleanup of the `pricing_rules` collection for TEST_ prefixed rules if a test aborts mid-run — self-heals on next successful run via delete step, but consider a class-scoped fixture with teardown.
